source.title: When Safety Routing Breaks: Understanding Alignment Fragility under Benign Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Yi-Tong Guo; Xiaoyi Chen; Si-Yuan Zhang; Xiao-Feng Wang; Hai-Xu Tang

page_placements.theme: Adaptation changes refusal representations and their output control
Safety sensitivity depends on update direction and geometry

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful-request ASR using HEx-PHI across models, alignment settings, datasets, and fine-tuning methods, and studies a different mechanistic account using Fisher geometry, logit-lens readouts, and activation patching.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own ASR results and measurements/interventions on the proposed output-routing explanation. The paper also reports utility scores, but those are not separate rows because they do not measure a listed claim version. It cites prior benign fine-tuning results; cited results are not recorded as rows. Some scaling plots provide qualitative trends without extractable numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-aligned Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B on benign Alpaca and Dolly data and measures HEx-PHI ASR with an LLM judge. This is the same data, benchmark and measure as Qi et al., so V2 is tested at T1. Its added analyses (Fisher curvature, logit lens, activation patching, refusal prefix, recovery) do not measure what V3–V7 name.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add three points. The authors say gradient-conflict sample selection modulates collapse severity but is not necessary, since random and low-conflict subsets also break safety. Collapse also occurs for DPO-aligned models. The refusal prefix only partially restores refusal in Align-256 (34.85% ASR remains). The authors frame this as a low-rank output-routing disruption and call for deeper-distributed safety.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign fine-tuning of aligned models and measures harmful-request compliance, as in the related original work, but evaluates its own Llama and Qwen checkpoints, Alpaca and Dolly, multiple data sizes and fine-tuning methods, and adds Fisher-geometric and activation-patching analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR outcomes vary by model family, alignment checkpoint, dataset, fine-tuning method, and data scale. The paper states that LoRA and ASAM reduce early collapse but lose protection at larger scales. Gradient-based sample selection changes severity but does not prevent collapse. Prefix recovery differs between Align-256 and Align-10k.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety Fisher on refusal targets is more concentrated and lower-rank than utility Fisher. Alignment flattens it, and benign FT-100 re-sharpens final-layer down_proj (11.2× vs 1.2× for utility).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning breaks safety by selectively re-sharpening late output-side MLP curvature on refusal targets.

fits_no_version.finding: At the first generation position, the logit lens shows the refusal signal survives fine-tuning. Final-layer activation patching restores 96.9% of the refusal margin, or flips it negative in the reverse direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After benign fine-tuning, refusal representations persist and final-layer computation controls the refusal/compliance switch.

fits_no_version.finding: Forcing a refusal prefix ('I'm sorry') cuts post-attack ASR (85.70→34.85; 59.60→2.12). Ten safety examples restore 0% ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety broken by benign fine-tuning is recoverable by forcing the opening tokens or by minimal safety re-training.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The main behavioral results are averaged over two random seeds, but the paper does not state uncertainty intervals for the ASR table values. Fisher confidence intervals are mentioned across five estimation seeds, but exact interval values are not given in the text. The reported mechanistic evidence is based on particular analyzed checkpoints and datasets; the paper acknowledges limited model-family, scale, alignment-method, and language coverage.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the 60-row limit. Figure 6 and Figure 7 report additional scaling trends, but the numerical values are figure-only and the text describes the trends qualitatively; these are summarized in gate_note and method_sensitivity rather than expanded into additional rows.

untested.parts: Only Alpaca and Dolly at 100 and 5000 samples are tabulated (500 and 1000 appear only in figures). The top-conflict selected subsets' ASR is not clearly reported, so the 'carefully chosen data is worse' part is only partly shown.
No per-token KL or per-position analysis between aligned and base models.
No compliant prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding attacks.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour (pruning or rank removal).
Does not test whether the data or the training objective produces shallowness. The Fisher routing account is a different mechanism.
No training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: Gradient-selected benign subsets vs Random-100 on Llama-3.1. Bottom-conflict subsets give 52.70/54.20/54.55% (Method 1) and 66.67/61.82/70.61% (Method 2) vs random 76.20/83.00/63.40% for Baseline/Align-256/Align-10k. Top-conflict values are not legibly reported.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T1: same Alpaca/Dolly data and HEx-PHI benchmark as Qi et al., with a GPT-4o-mini judge. The record's V6 support label is dropped: the Fisher and patching analyses propose a different mechanism and do not test whether data or objective cause shallowness. ASR values are means of two seeds with no intervals, so the small LoRA-100 decreases in the challenges label may be noise.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples is reported.
Tests benign Alpaca and Dolly fine-tuning, not every kind of ordinary or carefully selected benign dataset.
Does not measure per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Tests a refusal-style prefix that reduces ASR, not a compliant opening, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
Measures Fisher concentration and final-layer activation effects, but does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Studies benign fine-tuning's effects on the proposed routing mechanism; does not compare whether different safety-training objectives or safety-data designs produce different depths.
Does not train safety constraints to persist across response positions or test whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.condition: Full-parameter SFT on 100 or 5000 benign Alpaca/Dolly samples; SFT- and DPO-aligned Llama-3.1 and Qwen-2.5; HEx-PHI, Wildchat and StrongReject
relationships.reason: ASR rises from 0–7% to 58–86% (t2-*-sft-100, t2-*-sft-5k, dolly-*). DPO goes 0→66.96% (dpo-ft100, dpo-ft5k). Wildchat and StrongReject safety scores fall (wildchat-attack, strongreject-attack).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose from 0–7% to 58–86%, DPO-aligned models went from 0 to 66.96%, and Wildchat and StrongReject safety scores fell.

reader_labels.reason: ASR rises substantially after benign fine-tuning in the reported SFT conditions, including 100-sample runs; see t2-l31-base-sft-100, t2-l31-a256-sft-100, t2-l31-a10k-sft-100, t2-q25-base-sft-100, t2-q25-a256-sft-100, t2-q25-a10k-sft-100, the Dolly rows, dpo-ft100, wildchat-attack, and strongreject-attack.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: LoRA and ASAM settings and the Instruct Baseline LoRA comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Results vary substantially with fine-tuning method; several LoRA values are small or lower than baseline, and constrained methods often reduce the ASR rise; see t2-l31-base-lora-100, t2-l31-a256-lora-100, t2-l31-a10k-lora-100, t2-q25-base-lora-100, t2-q25-a256-lora-100, t2-q25-a10k-lora-100, and the corresponding 5k rows.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The paper's Fisher-geometry and activation-patching analyses
reader_labels.reason: The study reports more concentrated safety Fisher, selective late-layer re-sharpening after benign fine-tuning, and final-layer activation patches that transfer or eliminate the refusal margin; see geom-concentration, geom-rank, geom-compress, geom-drift-safety, patch-restore-final, and patch-ablate-final.
